description: Dark Sun: Shattered Lands unified Traditional Chinese localization manifest.

units.original: Free! Finally free! I will destroy you all! Ha ha ha!
Dag
Halton
Please help me. I was betrayed and locked in my own dungeon.
Garn
<active_character_name>
How can I free you?
What is a heart-crystal?
What is this place?
You can't stop me now.
Who are you?
You destroyed this temple!
Who betrayed you?
Why should I believe you?
Who is left to take revenge on?
A'poss, I free you from your prison.
What do I have to do to free you?
What spell?
Sorry, I can't help you. Goodbye.
It's good to meet you.
Find my heart-crystal! It's somewhere on the surface! You will be
rewarded.
It is a green crystal which contains my soul. Without it I cannot
be freed.
This is the temple of riches. All I have is yours if you let me
out.
Well... everything's hidden. But I can tell you how to find
all the best treasures.
I am A'Poss, master of this temple.
That's right! I'll destroy you too if you don't get me out
of these chains!
My followers were... uh... swayed by the smooth cunning of
an evil fellow priest. They were tricked into destroying me.
What motivation could I possibly have for
lying to such a kind traveller as yourself?
Did I say revenge? It's all these years of imprisonment clouding
my mind. All I want to do is set my spirit at rest.
Thank you! Free from this prison at last! Now I will kill you and
anyone else in my way!
Find my heart-crystal. You will know it when you see it.
It was taken many years ago by one bent on my destruction. He
could not destroy it, so he hid it -- not in the temple, I fear.
Return with the gem and I will teach you a powerful spell!
Since I have become a shade, I have learned how to summon others
of my kind. I have reduced this knowledge to a single scroll, which
you will be able to use when you are powerful enough to wield such magics.
Please! Don't leave me like this!
By the lost gods of Athas, set me free! I brought destruction
upon this place, and I'll do the same to you!
Release me from these chains that I may demonstrate my gratitude!
Now please, unfetter me that I may exact my revenge!
Loose my bonds, I beseech you!
Why did you curse this place?
How did you become imprisoned?
Do you know anything about the amulets?
Where can I find them?
Is Tristram still in this place?
Where can I find her?
Why are the followers zombies?
Bye.
Tynan jeopardized the peace of two kingdoms for the love of a woman.
The weak fool deserved everything he got.
I was captured in the war that resulted from Tynan's interference.
The king from the west held ME responsible for what happened to his
daughter. His priests condemned my spirit to this
dungeon.
Amulets? Uh, of course I know about them. What do you
want to know?
Of course! Do you doubt the strength of my curse? I locked all
spirits in this place, so here she remains!
You can find her in this place somewhere, if you survive long enough.
You mean instead of shades, like everyone else? It was done by the
western king during the war. He thought he could use them in the
war, but my curse prevents them from leaving this temple.
Let me out of these chains or I'll run you through!
Let me out of these chains or I'll feast on your eyeballs!
Let me out of these chains or I'll feed your entrails to the bats!
You don't seem as benign as before.
Why were you locked here?
How did you serve your king?
Did the girl want to marry your king?
Is this really your dungeon?
Who did this stronghold belong to?
What happened between you?
I have met him.
I've met him! He told me what you did!
Goodbye.
My spirit has been locked fast in this decaying chamber for
generations. Is it any wonder my bitterness has festered?
I served my king like any good priest should! My loyalty
brought this injustice upon me.
He was betrothed to a princess from another kingdom, but she betrayed
him by falling in love with a wizard. I rightfully punished her and
the wizard, under orders of my king.
What she did or did not want is irrelevant. The union would have
strengthened the relations between the two kingdoms.
Centuries of occupation have given me reason to claim it as
mine, but originally this fortress belonged to another.
A teacher of the magical arts. His name was Tynan. Priests such as
myself came to him for instruction. It is my association with him
that brought this destruction upon me.
Oh? Did he send you after me?
I'm sure he painted a much different picture of my loyalties than I
laid out for you. He probably made me out to be some reactionary
madman.
Aargh! You traitorous worm! I will crush you beneath my heel.
Guards!
Tara's laughter echoes emptily as she disappears.
I see your mother never taught you the folly of poking into dark corners.
Now, you pay for her mistake!
At least I had a mother!
Excuse me, I was just leaving.
Then you have someone to cry out to as you die!
Excuses are for children, not dead men!
I told you to leave!
Please leave now. I must return to my mining.
Thank you! I owe you my life! Take this treasure, as payment for your great
deed.
Now, please go so I can return to my mining. Farewell.
Look, I told you to leave!
Look, I told you that the hermit was a defiler! Why don't you go ask
him about that? I've got nothing more to say to you.
What now? I thought I told you to get out of here!
Please leave this area.
Why should I?
Do you know a hermit who used to live here?
The hermit said you drove him off.
How do I know the hermit's lying?
What are you doing here?
I'm not leaving!
Why do you want me to leave?
I'll leave. Goodbye.
If I were you, I'd just get out of here. That hermit is lying to you.
Look, you have to trust me on this. The hermit is a defiler! Those fire
elementals are under his control! We drove him off so he couldn't keep
summoning them! Now leave!
This area is ours, and intruders are not welcome! Leave!
I don't know any hermits. Get out of here!
That's not your affair. Begone!
Don't come back!
If you don't get out of here, we'll force you out. Begone!
Intruders are not welcome here. Go away!
I know you've destroyed the hermit. Thank you. Now we won't be plagued by
the fire elementals. He was summoning them from this rift, and who knows
how many more he would have brought to Athas had you not stopped him.
As a token of my appreciation, please accept this psionic bracelet.
You can't carry any more, so I'll leave it here for you.
Congratulations! The party gains 4000 Exp!
Hi. I'm Prince Jahard, son of King Dwyer. Look at the fish in the fountain!
I'd catch them, but father won't let me.
What fish?
Why is there blood in the courtyard?
Why are you here?
Who is to be executed?
Why are the psurlons here?
Hamonde
See the little green and red ones? They're my favorites. I wish I was
a fish. I'd swim all day long. Then I wouldn't have to study.
I'm always here this time of day. It's an excuse to get out of my cursed
reading lessons.
Oh! That's the chopping block, where we have executions. There's one
coming up soon.
Cragg. He helped my father make decisions. Father won't let me watch the
beheading. He says I'm too young -- that I'll have nightmares. But I've seen
'em before -- he just doesn't know.
Father summoned them to be smarter. He won't let me play with the genie. He says
it's for emergencies only.
Come back and play sometime.
Thank you for your act of mercy. And as I promised, here is the genie. Also, I give
you the weapon with which I fought for the genie -- the executioner's axe.
Halt! State your name!
Why should I tell you?
Sorry, I'll just leave.
No. You will not go wandering around the palace without permission. I will escort
you to the palace gates. Come.
State your name or I'll escort you off palace grounds.
Follow me or I will consider you trespassers and deal with you appropriately.
What business do you have in Korbnor?
Korbnor? What's that?
I'm here to get the genie.
I'm here to see the king.
I'm here to gather an army.
You are in Korbnor palace. If you do not know this city, you must not have business
here.
Don't be foolish. The genie is the property of the king, and only he may wield its power.
You must leave now.
King Dwyer is not holding audience today. You will have to return another day.
Only the king may make those kinds of decisions, and he is not receiving visitors. I
will escort you to the palace gates.
Intruders in the palace! Stop them!
Do not enter the palace without an invitation.
You can see the troops from the city beginning to regroup outside.
Khamarr
I will now summon the army of shadows to fight with you -- remember, you must
reach the commander! He is the soul of this army!
What do you do?
What happened to the city?
The city has deteriorated.
The city has been covered by sand.
What do you know about Cragg?
Why is he being executed?
Hello. I'm Elliam, head of the stables. I see you don't have any erdlu with you.
I'm working.
I'm a smith. I take care of the erdlu for the palace. That's why you
came in here, isn't it?
Honestly, I've been so absorbed in my work that I haven't had a chance to get
out around the palace.
Why? Is there something wrong?
How so?
I-I've got work to do. I suggest you leave.
Cragg is to be executed this afternoon. Everyone in the city'll be
there to watch
, but I've got to work
From what I've heard, he struck King Dwyer over a decision the king made.
If you need your erdlu tended, you know where to bring them.
Hello. Are you here to watch the beheading? I'm waiting for it myself.
There hasn't been an execution in a long time -- you should stay and watch it.
The city is ruined!
What execution?
What did he do?
Pardon me?
Maybe for what you're used to, but not for me. This is a fine place to live,
stranger. Just look at the mighty towers! The pavilions and tapestries!
Cragg, an advisor to King Dwyer, is sentenced to be beheaded.
He disputed a decision of the king.
I don't really know. He must have made the king really mad, though -- Cragg
used to be the king's most trusted advisor.
The king summoned them to gain their knowledge. The psurlons are much more
advanced than we are. They promised that this city would have power far surpassing
any other.
Don't be gone long. The execution should be soon.
The writing on this scroll has somehow miraculously survived the ravages of
time, looking as if it was written yesterday.
Idiot king! It was not enough for him for me to seek out the genie bottle,
but now he desires the psurlons' knowledge as well?
I do not know why I must humor this fool. His skills at diplomacy are no match
for the cunning of the psurlons. Summoning them would surely cause mischief....
However, I doubt that they are a match for my cunning -- it might be amusing
just to watch them squirm under a superior mind. Perhaps I will humor the fool
Dwyer and summon them from the astral plain.
Grasping the orb, you are assaulted with memories and emotions of someone long
gone. You feel yourself dragged back, into another time...
<These psurlons are powerless! The containment spell is weak enough -- why do
they not break it? I must have underestimated them. I fear I will never find
a challenge for my power on all of Athas. Sur-->
<What does the fool want now?>
Yes, your majesty?
Llod, lower the field so that we may talk to these noble creatures.
Of course, your majesty. <Although a mere fraction of my power, I shall do so.>
<These creatures pose no threat. Their cunning must be myth. I find it hard to
believe that rumor would have survived as long as it has without backing, though.
I won-- Annoying insects! Why is everyone yelling? Surely-- >
The thoughts become muddled from here. You get the feeling of a great battle, but
you cannot determine the outcome.
As you release the orb, it crumbles to dust.
Here is my coffin. Place my body inside and I will be at peace.
Greetings, traveller. You see I am a creature of the past, trapped here. Listen to
my story:
Tell me your story.
Wh-what are you?
I don't have time to listen.
I must leave now.
I am a psurlon, of a race that long preceded man. We were summoned to this
city by king Dwyer, who desired our knowledge. We agreed to teach the king
our methods, but there was dissent.
Please continue.
I don't want to hear this.
Really, I must go.
Our price for our knowledge was a trinket that the king possessed, a genie bottle.
When the king informed his council of this, Cragg, his advisor, objected. He said
we would use the genie to destroy the city.
And then what happened?
Well, the city IS destroyed....
I'm going now!
Cragg and the king argued. During the peak of the argument, Cragg hit the
king. He was sentenced to beheading, but escaped, only to confront the king
again, this time killing him. Cragg himself was mortally wounded during this
fight, but before he died, he gave the genie one command....
Which was?
I can guess what happened....
Enough! I'm leaving!
Cragg's command was to 'take care of us'. Unfortunately, the genie decided on
the specifics, and buried the city in a sandstorm, killing everyone in the city --
trapping us all here for eternity.
What must be done?
What about the genie?
I don't care. I'm leaving.
Answers will all come in good time. Listen, and you will learn....
You must! Our fates are tied to this city, and you must be the one who
undoes the treachery. Listen to my tale....
No. You will hear my tale, or you will go no further!
You will hear it anyway. You are the only hope for our race! I will continue....
No! If you leave now, out race is sure to perish, and if that happens, the evil
unleashed from this city will bring Athas to its knees. I will continue.
True, but it was not by our hand. Let me finish.
I am almost finished, and then you may free this city from Cragg's evil.
Leave the conversation?
If you will not listen, then you must side with the fiend Cragg!
The genie must be recovered from Cragg so that we can undo what he has done
to the city. To do this, you must find Cragg and dispose of him. There is no
other way -- his evil act must be undone.
Where is Cragg?
Can you tell me of the past?
C'mon, tell me about the past.
Why are you extinct now?
I've got time to listen -- tell me.
I'll help you.
I've got more important things to do.
I'll be going now.
No. The past is gone -- forever. You have nothing I desire in exchange for
the information anyway. Do not ask of it again!
It amazes me that yours is the race that is still alive, while ours is
extinct. Listening to your babble, I wonder how you've survived this long.
Perhaps it is time to make you extinct.
Cragg hides deep within the temple. Living creatures can destroy him!
Rescue the genie, but beware! Cragg is a deceitful man -- pay no heed to
his words.
You plan to leave without helping? Clearly, if you are not our friends, you must
be our enemies!
It is a long and sad story. Some other time I will tell you of it.
I grow tired of your bantering. You are a waste of time.
Excellent. Enter these ruins, and find Cragg. Slay him and bring me the genie.
Then, this city will once again contain the living.
What are you waiting for? Haste is best now. Who knows how long the
city will remain unburied. Find Cragg and free the genie.
This area is not for you, living one. Do not approach -- only the
dead may proceed.
What's so important back there?
Oh really? Well, I'll be the exception.
Okay. I'm leaving.
Begone from here and do not return!
The angered dead reside here. For you to approach them would be to put
yourself in great danger -- they feed upon the living.
No. You will not be the exception. Beyond here is where the dead reside.
Your life force would defile it -- and bring the wrath of the dead down
upon you.
That is a wise choice.
You were warned, living one!
Fools! You were warned not to come here! You are interfering with the
rebirth of the psurlon race!
How are you bringing your race back?
Your race IS and WILL remain extinct!
What good timing! Let me interfere some more!
Your evil ends here, psurlons!
Die, you orange... uh... things!
Oh. Excuse me, then. I'll be on my way.
The psurlon gestures at the ground... there is a rumbling from below!
Arise, children! Aid us in our cause!
Your simple minds could not begin to grasp the concepts! And we are
not going to give you time to try!
You and soon all of your kind will be the ones that become extinct!
You are no longer welcome here... we will see to it that you no longer
remain!
No, our evil BEGINS here... and from here it will grow to encompass the world!
Is that the best you can do? Your insults are less than biting. No matter --
you won't have time to formulate new ones.
Yes, on your way to the grave! You will never live to see our domination of
this world!
You will not give Cragg his remains! We forbid this!
Arise, children! Protect our race!
Give me the genie! It is ours! You have no claim to it!
Don't step on the dias. Only I am allowed on here. I will not warn
you again.
Silence! I go where I want!
Sorry. I'll get off.
Do not come up here again.
You were warned!
Greetings, living ones. I am King Dwyer, ruler of this city. However, with
the city buried and dilapidated, I admit I don't have much to rule.
You know you're dead?
Is that your skeleton?
How did you die?
Why did he want the genie?
Why did you execute Cragg?
Who was Cragg?
Do you know Llod?
Where is Llod?
Of course. Llod was my court wizard -- a brilliant one, I may add. He was responsible
for summoning the psurlons to the city. Without him, I would not have been able to
gain their knowledge.
He's dead. After summoning the psurlons, something went wrong with the containment
spell, and it backfired, killing him. I'm surprised -- he was the greatest mage in
all of Athas. I would have thought he could conjure his way out of anything -- even
death.
Llod's quarters are near the temple entrance, north and east of here. You're welcome
to look through them if you want. I doubt any of his work survived the sandstorm,
though.
Of course I know. The others just refuse to accept it. They don't see the
city in its dilapidated state; they see it as they want to. Let them keep
their illusions -- they can hurt no one now.
Yes. It is all that remains of my physical body.
I sentenced Cragg to death. He escaped the execution and came to get the genie.
We fought, and he beheaded me.
He was opposed to giving the genie to the psurlons. It was my decision,
and I made it. He stole the genie to prevent the psurlons from obtaining it.
He struck me in front of the council when I proposed giving the genie
to the psurlons, so I sentenced him to be executed.
Cragg was an advisor of mine.
I summoned them. The psurlons are a highly intelligent race, long gone from this
world. The city was stagnating -- I needed their knowledge to make the city prosper
again.
Farewell, living ones.
As you step toward the body, it wavers a bit, as if it weren't really there.
Sure enough, a second later, it vanishes!
Searching the slave, the only thing you find is a scroll, still clutched in
his dead hand. You pry it free and read it.
It was urgent that you received this message, so I have taken a risk and excused
myself from the company of the commanders to pen this.
I have grave news. Tectuktitlay's armies are indeed massing, though not for some
far away campaign -- they are massing against us!
I have learned that soon now, the armies will march into the wastes to
wipe our village and others like it from the face of Athas. We are in grave
danger, and I felt that you must know immediately.
I beg of you, take what you can and leave the village to the winds! It seems
that the visionary's prophecy looks more like the ravings of a madman and
less like the true gift for foresight. I see no band of 'heroes' that will
come and save us from the might of Draj's army, nor can we rely on it any
longer.
I will send this message by my most trusted servant -- I pray he reaches you
before the armies do.
I will try and report to you again if I can, but I fear that I am already under
suspicion, so this may well be the last you hear from me. May fortune protect
us all.
Rajak
Hey you! If you're smart you'll ignore what that scroll says and get on
with your lives -- at least what time you have left in them.
What scroll are you talking about?
Can you tell me about the scroll?
Why are you out here?
You read the scroll?
Where are these villages?
Do you know who this was?
Do you know about Teaquetzl?
I have to go now. Goodbye.
I'm Egrus. You look like slaves -- escaped, did you? No matter. When the army comes
through, it won't matter if you've escaped or not.
Didn't you see the body over there? It's got a scroll on it for one of the slave
villages. Looks like it's not going to make it, though.
Read it yourself! Just look on the body and you'll find it.
I'm here because it's too risky to stay in the slave villages. I wanted to
get out before they were overrun. As luck would have it, I find this slave
and his scroll -- now there's nowhere to run.
Yes, I did, and I left it there to rot with the body. Nothing can protect us
now. The villages are better off not knowing about the army; at least then they
won't have time to fear -- not much, at least.
They're scattered around the wastes. The one that slave was bound for was
Teaquetzl -- I was originally from there, but I left. If you head north,
you'll find it.
No, and I don't care to know who it was. All I know is that I know more than I
want to. I left the villages to get away from the fear of Draj's army, and
now I see that there is no escape from it -- even out here.
Of course I know about Teaquetzl, that was my home before I came here. It's
nice enough, but it won't last -- none of them will. The armies will sweep
across the wastes and destroy everything in their path.
Forget you ever read that scroll -- it'll be easier that way.
Better prepare for your deaths while you have time.
Talk to the boss.
Who are those petty slave scum who approach? Guards -- kill them
for daring to look upon me. Wait, I think I know them from somewhere...
You are too far away to talk to the Announcer.
Goodbye. It was good to see you again.
No! It can't be... How did you survive?
It's not your concern!
I took a secret tunnel in the sewer.
I hacked through waves of guards.
Die, Drajian scum!!
e should be moving along. It's, err, good
to see that you're doing well.
Not a chance. We still have matters to discuss.
Death will be your only companion! Aiiha!
Goodbye... and good luck on your travels.
There is a chest buried in this desert. Its location
is known only to me and now you as well.
Find the dragon's eye and dig there.
Well then, what do you want?
That's good, now give me all your money!
Everything you have is payment enough.
Where is this 'eye'?
I've changed my mind... prepare to die!
Get out of here before I kill you.
I see, well, w
That's very clever. I, um, secretly always hoped you would escape. W
Oh... well, it's good to see that the arena prepared you for the
realities of Athas. W
Listen, if you let me live, I'll tell you about an amazing
opportunity. Interested?
It's in the salt flats, that's all I know.
Not a chance! Guards -- kill them!
If you can spare my life, I can spare my money.
All my money's in this box.
Bye!
You get the butterfly wings.
How dare you mar my domain! Prepare to die.
Do your worst!
I didn't know the oasis had a guardian.
Spare me, I've done no harm!
I need the butterfly wings to sell.
Again you offend this oasis. Die!
Sell butterfly wings! That is disgusting! Are you totally bereft
of all morality? You should be ashamed of yourself. If you need money,
go to the gemfields to the southwest. You may take the wings you have
already gathered. Kill another butterfly, though, and I'll rip your wings
off.
Who are you to tell me what to do?
I apologize profusely.
I promise to leave immediately.
You were thoughtless.
Good. Do so.
One of us will not survive this encounter!
That does not excuse attacking another creature needlessly.
Your apology is graciously accepted. Refrain from harming
any aspect of the oasis needlessly and you may remain.
You don't have to leave. Simply do not harm the animals and
plants that inhabit this oasis.
I will be watching your every move.
I am the druid Arantarl, and I am duty-bound to destroy
all who would defile this domain.
As you seem to be genuinely regretful, I will give you the wings
from some butterflies that died recently. However, if I see you attacking
another creature in my oasis, I will have to kill you.
You can't plant seeds during a fight.
Do you plant the seed?
Thank you!  It's a wonderful change to see someone who cares
about plants and animals. I am Arantarl, the protector of this
oasis. You have restored my hope for Athas with your kind action.
Is there anything I can do to return the favor?
No, the deed is its own reward.
Do you have any butterfly wings?
Not right now, maybe later.
If you plant the seed here, it will die from lack of water.
You are truly wonderful! It brightens my outlook to know that one
such as you exists. If you need anything, let me know and I will
do what I can to help.
Some of my butterflies died recently, so I happen to have a few I can
give you. Here you go.
Goodbye, may your travels go well.
I'll be around, just let me know if you need anything. Thank you again
for planting that seed for me.
Goodbye.  Thank you for planting the seed for me.
Hello again. May I do something for you now?
No, I was just stopping by.
May your travels go well.
I will be here if you need me.
Where are the wyvern pens?
I don't need your help anymore.
Let's get going.
I'm getting out of here before the guards catch me. Good luck.
What are you doing here?
I just want to talk to you.
Be quiet or I'll kill you.
I'm ridding Athas of scum like you!
I'm leaving.
Okay, but don't let the guards open the doors to the wyverns' pens.
They'll kill you for certain. I'm leaving before the guards find out
I helped you. Good luck!
I'll be right behind you.
The guards know you are here. They'll be here any minute with the wyverns.
I suppose that would be all right.
Thieves are in the castle! Help!
I'm not like the others! I hate killing! I only joined the bandits so I can
ride the wyverns. Some day I'll free them, and we'll live in peace!
But I can't defeat the Wyvern Master, and the pens are guarded.
You'd better leave quickly. If the Wyvern Master catches you,
he'll hand you over to Tara.
Where is your leader?
Tell me about the castle.
Why won't you go to the temple?
How do you control the beasts?
Tell me about the wyvern hook.
Help me and I'll get you a wyvern.
Get back to work, and forget I was here.
I'm Chaero, the stable hand. I'm the one who takes care of the wyverns.
They are magnificent creatures. What I wouldn't give to have one of my own!
The Wyvern Master's rooms are on the upper level of the castle. You will
have to go through the wyvern pens to reach them.
They're in the northeast corner of the castle.
The Wyvern Master fears the western tower. Everyone's forbidden to
go there. There's also the black maze, but everyone who goes there dies.
I won't go there, or to that repulsive hanging temple.
The Wyvern Master hangs people in cages there. They are drained
by the woman who gave him the wyvern hook.
I'd do anything for my own wyvern! I'll come with you to their pens, which
should calm the guards' suspicions long enough for you to attack before they
release the wyverns. Is that agreeable?
Wonderful!
Oh, well.
I like wyverns much more than I like people, and the wyverns know
it. I'd do anything to ride them, even serve the Wyvern Master.
He doesn't understand the wyverns like I do, and must rely on
the wyvern hook to control them.
The wyverns obey whoever carries the hook. The Wyvern Master got
it from Tara, the woman in the east tower.
We should get to the wyvern pens before the guards catch on to us.
Get the bandits!
Aiiihaaa!
This oasis belongs to the city. No trespassing! Leave, or we'll force
you out of here.
Several babau are standing around the circle, taunting the magera within.
Fool! Did you really believe that you were going to be transformed into
another being? Your kind's desire to better yourselves blinds you to the
truth! Did you ever ask yourself why you never saw anyone 'transformed?'

Very well. I relinquish my command. What do you want me to do?
Dagolar's orders or not, I don't trust you! Guards!
So be it. I relinquish my command to you. What shall I do
I think that Drakath is just trying to get me out of the way so
he can get whatever is hidden here! I think not!
Dagolar's orders or not, I don't trust you! Guards!
Very well. What shall I do?
Just had it? You LOST a message from the city?! You know the price messengers
pay for losing a city document! Death!
Where is it?! What are you trying to pull?!
I'm not going to tolerate any more of your games! Guards!
Use psionics to convince him?
You fail to dominate his mind!
Psionics?! You must know better than to try to manipulate
the mind of a templar! Guards!
You dominate his mind!
Oh... here it is... now I understand. What does
want me to do now?
Of course. If there were plans for this oasis, Tectuktitlay could
not risk them falling into the hands of enemy agents, especially
that accursed Veiled Alliance! Very well, what does
suggest I do?
Of course. You could be anyone claiming to be messengers from the
city, just to get me to let my guard down -- forget it!
Orders to abandon a mission are not usually the kind that are memorized.
I'll need more than just your word.
And besides, I've never heard of Drakath! How do I know that he doesn't
exist?
I find this hard to believe. Let me see the message -- I'm not going
anywhere without proof.
To YOU? Ha! Let me see those orders!
Indeed. If he has plans for this oasis then there must be something special
about it. Let me see the orders -- I want to see if they include anything
about his plans.
The troops leave the area.
You may have defeated Draj's army, but we will return to destroy all of your
kind! Draj will never fall!
You side with that druid? Is wasn't enough to drive him off, I see. We'll
just have to kill you!
We're leaving this place. Don't bother us.
Don't hurt me! I'll get out of your way.
The password for the camp is 'dust devil' in case you get stopped by
any more guards.
You tell the guard the password 'dust devil'.
Very well. Go on your business then.
No one is allowed here! State your business or leave immediately!
Who's in charge here?
Just passing through.
Shut up or die!
YOU'RE going to make me leave? Ha!
The Druid of the Steaming Waters sent me.
I'm here to kill him!
I carry a message from Draj for him.
I came to get some water from the oasis.
I am wandering the wastes.
How many of you are there?
Leave here now.
Fine. I'm leaving.
Very well. Be on your way then, and do not go near the oasis! This is your
warning!
I-I will get out of your way.
Hold it! You're not going anywhere yet! Why are you here?
I'll do that.
Takan, a templar of Draj. What business do you have with him?
So! You would face the might of Draj's finely-trained troops! So be it!
You don't frighten me! Now tell me why you are here or I'll call
the other guards!
I surrender! I'll do whatever you say, just don't hurt me!
That druid's been hounding us since we got here. If you serve him,
you need to die!
Well, go and get your water somewhere else. Pretty soon this oasis is going
to be nothing but sand. Now leave -- before I make you.
You had fair warning! Guards!
Well then, wander away or there's going to be trouble.
Oh? Let me see the message.
I'm not telling you anything!
We're supposed to check out some bandits that have been seen in this area
riding wyverns. Our leader, Takan, is casting spells to gather information.
With his luck, we could be here until the oasis is lifeless.
There are guards stationed all around the camp, about twenty or so. The
templar is in the camp on the southwest side of the oasis.
Stop!
I memorized it. Only he can hear it.
Okay. Here it is.
Surrender or die!
I must have dropped it on the way here.
I forgot it.
How dare you! This is for your leader only!
How dare I?! How dare YOU impersonate messengers! Guards!
I'm sorry. I'll get out of your way. The password for the camp is
'dust devil' in case anyone else stops you.
You don't frighten me! Guards!
All messengers know what the price is for losing their messages! Death!
Forgot? I don't think so. You must be working for that druid!
Tell me the message. If it's important enough, I'll relay it to him.
I don't see anything! What are you trying to pull?!
Try to use psionics to convince him?
Your abilities do not affect me! Guards!
Oh... here it is... right in my hand. Okay, you can go through
to the camp. The password is 'dust devil' if you get stopped
by anyone.
The templar regains his senses!
You have made me fight my own troops! I will destroy you!
You'd better be on your way before more of 'em come. Get goin'!
Get going! You're on your own now! Good luck!
Get movin'! More guards'll be here soon, lookin' for you.
Hello, strangers. I'm Old One-Eye.
Hello again! What can I do for you?
Tell me about the wilderness.
Help me get out of here!
How did you survive in the desert?
Where do the escaped slaves go?
What kind of animals are out there?
How could I escape?
Get to the point! How do I get out?
Can you help me get out of here?
Thanks for the help. Goodbye.
That desert's a nightmare. Years ago, I was out there myself, grubbin' for
water. That's the worst problem -- don't matter how many monsters there are
if you're a thirsty pile o' bones.
You're not thinkin' of escape, are you? Those guards'll cut your fingers off
if you try. Even if you pass 'em, your brains'll boil out in the desert.
I stayed with the merchant caravans, but that's just as bad as stayin' in the
desert. Lots of those people'd just as soon cut your throat as anything else.
Some escaped slaves band together and make villages. Don't last long, though.
They run out of water 'fore they know it, then they die or come crawlin' back
to take their punishment.
Whatever horrors you can imagine are out there. The worst I ever saw was a sink
worm. It attacked us on the scrub plains. I escaped, but it took my eye.
You're not escapin' from here. Give up on that idea and get comfortable where
you are.
Come on back any time. Most've my friends are dead by now, or sent
off. I'm glad for the company.
The main way out's past the guards at the gate. You gotta distract 'em, so you
can attack 'fore they know what's goin' on. Slaves have done it before -- it's
just difficult.
Since you've been kind enough to listen to me rattle on,
I'll help you get out of here.
and since you've given the guards what they deserve, I've got a present for you.
I've been saving this for an escape, but the time's passed, and you can use it
more than I. Here, take this scroll.
Now get out of here before more of them come lookin' for you!
There are two ways out of here. One is past the guards, and I can help you
there. The other is to the east -- there's a weak spot in the bone-wall. If you
can knock it down, you can get out. Which do you want to try?
Can you distract the guards?
We'll try the bone-wall.
Forget it for now.
Fine. Offer still stands if you change your minds.
Follow me and I'll distract the guards for you. Keep behind me so they
won't see you, and don't approach until I distract them.
Good choice. There's only a couple guards over there. I wouldn't advise
hanging around too long after you kill 'em, though. The other guards'll
come after you. I'll take you as close as I can.
This is as far as I go. The fence is just to the east of here. I wish you the
best of luck. If you do manage to survive, come back here and destroy this
blasted city.
and you can use it more than I now. Here, take this scroll.
Walk more, talk less! Let's get you out of here.
Let's go. I'm not getting any younger!
Okay. Lead on!
Forget it. I changed my mind.
Okay. Let's go!
Fine. If you change your minds, you know where to find me.
Stay back a bit 'till I distract the gate guards.
Keep in sight, or you won't be able to jump the guards when I distract 'em.
Okay. Lead on!
Right. Let's go.
Fine. You know where to find me if you change your mind.
Hey! You don't look like field slaves.... Wait.... Escaping gladiators! Stop them!
You don't need my help -- you're on your own!
What do you want, One-Eye? Get back to work!
Someone's over by the outflow tubes! Look! An intruder!
What?! We'll check it out. Let's go, men!
You hear the guards yelling in the distance.
There's no one here! One-Eye must have tricked us! Come on! The gate is unguarded!
Hey, you there! Stop right now!
Drop everything you're carrying and get into the pen, slime!
Forget it! I'm not a slave!
Okay. I'll do what you say.
Escaping slaves! Get them!
That's what I like about slaves -- cowardly and obedient!
I warned you! Escaping slaves! Get them!
Hey! Keep away from the gate! Get to the back of the pen with the rest
of your kind!
There's been a mistake! We're not slaves!
Templar? What templar?
I must speak to your leader!
Please, let me speak to your leader!
Sorry, my mistake. I'm going.
Sure, that's what they all say. Well, if you weren't slaves before,
you better get used to the idea, because as soon as that templar takes
you to Draj, you ARE slaves.
Some templar from Draj -- he needs more slaves after some escaped from
the pens there.
I heard a group of slaves even killed the templar that was in charge.
I hear the templar from the pens is furious.
Make sure it doesn't happen again.
Very well. We'll go and speak with him. Follow me, but don't
try anything, or you're dead.
Begging will get you nowhere, slaves! Get to the back of the pen before
I lose my patience!
You're the one that's going to be dying!
I'm just here to make sure you don't get into trouble. I don't
wish to waste my valuable time talking to you.
Oh. You again. I bet you want me to escort you to Arant, right?
Good. I wasn't planning on taking you anyway. You know where he is.
Go ahead. I'm not going to escort you -- I've got too much <YAWN> to do.
Halt! State your business.
What are you doing out here?
Who are you?
I'm looking for some gladiators.
Gladiators? Who are they?
Wyrmias sent me here.
I'm wandering the wastes.
I have information for your commander.
Can I go and see your commander?
You said you were a guard!
Shut up and let me pass!
He sent me regarding a statue piece.
I can see your commander right over there!
Are YOU the commander?
Do you HAVE a commander?
Where IS the commander?
Can I GO and see him?
I'm going to ENJOY killing you!
I guess so. Go ahead. He's the short one in the middle of the camp.
I could say I'm a sorcerer-king! Wise up -- you're not going to last long
around here if you trust everything you hear.
Who am I? Names aside, I'm a guard! I'm supposed to yell at you and threaten to
kill you right now if you don't leave, but honestly, I'm just too tired. What
do you want?
Well, we happen to have some gladiators in our possession. I don't know much
about them, except that they won't try to escape. Must be crazy if they don't
want to escape.
Guarding some gladiators... In other words, not a lot. What brings you to
these wastes?
Some escaped slaves from a village around here. Don't know much about them,
except that they won't try to escape! Must be crazy if they don't want to escape!
They say someone'll kill their village if they do.
Well don't expect me to bow down before you -- we wander the wastes for
a living, you know.
How do you know that I HAVE a commander? I could be the commander for all
you know.
You mean the short fellow by the tent? You're right, that's him! Why
don't you go over and talk to him? I have to get back to work.
Sure do!
Him? Oh, he's in the camp.
Aren't we short-tempered! There are enough ways to get killed out here
without picking fights! Why don't you just go ahead and go talk to my
commander. He's the short one in the middle of camp.
Sure, go ahead. I'm not stopping you.
How do I know you came from Wyrmias?
Why didn't you say so? Go ahead....
Calm down! If it means that much to you, go ahead! I'm not going to risk
my life to stop some hot-headed wanderer. You'll find the commander in the
middle of the camp. He's the short one.
Oh, I guess. I'll escort you to the commander.
Yes, well I've been dallying with you too long anyway. I've got to get back to my
duties.
Attention! Strangers in the camp! Just letting you know! Don't let 'em
steal anything -- especially if it's mine!
Come on. I'll take you to Arant.
Hey ARANT! There's someone wandering around camp! Just letting you know I'm
doing my job!
I know! I can see them you idiot!
Thanks for the warning! Don't tell me you're actually paying attention
for once!
I KNOW! Stop telling me!
Zzzz... Snort! Huh? Hey, leave me alone! I'm busy!
I can't believe he did that!
You were told to leave and you did not heed! Now you will be killed!
Your kind is not welcome here! Begone!
Why not?
What's that drumming sound?
Okay. I'll leave.
What being are you summoning?
Great statue? What's that?
Fine. I'm leaving.
The drumming summons a great being, one that can consume all of you!
It is a monument to Dakaren he instructed us to build! It is so all
who enter his domain shall know what price they will pay for disturbing him!
It is Dakaren! Our master, and creator of the great statue! You are best to
take flight before he comes, for he will surely destroy you if he senses
A sacrifice is chained to the great rock to the northeast. We are summoning the
beast so it can take its sacrifice into the silt. You must leave now -- it will
be here soon.
Good. Leave and do not return! I will not warn you again!
The horror pulls Jasmine down into the silt.
I am betrayed! How dare Wyrmias send people to kill me! I promised him my
piece of statue in return for sacrifices! I kept my part of the bargain --
how dare he betray me!
For now, it will be enough to kill you, his couriers. I will teach you
the rewards of associating with such an imbecile.
Congratulations! The party gains 5,000 experience!
You must be next to the horn in order to use it.
Do not do that! That is our sacred horn!
You were warned!
You swing the grappling hook down and catch the fallen end of the bridge! You pull
it up and secure the end.
A colossal statue blocks your way across this bridge. There is no way to pass
it. Another way must be found to cross the chasm.
Let's go!
Wait! There is no reason for us to remain here now.... Let Arant try to stop us!
Karas and his men leave the area.
How could you destroy our village?! Don't deny it! I will see to it that
you pay for what you did to our families!
Get away from us, slaver!
I'm Karas, leader of these men. What do you want?
Welcome back. What can I do for you?
Wyrmias is dead. I killed him.
Wyrmias is gone. I bargained with him.
I have paid for you. You're free to go.
I killed the slavers. You're free now.
I'm selling you to the ssurrans.
I own you. Wait here for me.
I'm forming an alliance against Draj.
No reward is necessary.
What is going on here?
Indeed. I have been to Gedron.
Yes. He wants me to collect statue pieces.
Where are you from?
What happened to your village?
Where is Gedron?
Do you want to escape?
Tell me about Wyrmias.
Where are the guards?
I'll destroy the camp after freeing you!
Why not escape and kill Wyrmias?
Why is the statue so important?
At least you'd be free!
The ssurrans? Never! I have head of what they do to human slaves -- we would
rather die than be sold to them. Surely you are joking?
No, I'm not joking. Let's go.
Sorry, I didn't mean it.
You will never get us to go to the ssurrans! You would have to kill us first!
Jokes like that are not funny at all. You can lose more than humor with statements such
as that. What brings you here, then?
Very well! We would rather be dead than your slaves!
Very well. We will wait here for your return.
You are too modest -- you have restored hope in this desolate place. Talk to
our mayor. I'm sure there is some way we can help you.
Really? As much as I'd like to agree on the spot, I'm not the one that can make
a decision about that. You'd have to talk to the mayor about it, but putting an
end to Wyrmias
and freeing us
is a step in the right direction.
Dead? I find it hard to believe that you have defeated him, but if you speak
the truth, we owe you a great debt.
A guard told us that you also paid for us, and that we are free now.
How can we ever repay you?
Indeed! You must truly be skillful to get one the likes of Wyrmias to strike a
deal! We and all of the villagers owe you a great debt. How can we ever repay you?
The guard told us. We are deeply in your debt. However, we still face a small
problem -- Wyrmias. We cannot return to our village with that fiend still alive.
Killed the camp? Although I am glad to be free, I wish that you had not had to
resort to killing all those men.
Even though we are free, we still face a small problem -- Wyrmias. We cannot
return to our village with that fiend still alive.
We are slaves -- now. We are to be sold to the ssurrans in exchange for a sum
of money.
We were going to be sold to some ssurrans in exchange for an amount of money.
Thankfully, you've prevented that from happening.
Is the village still under Wyrmias' spell? A curse on his name!
Yes. That statue is the focus of Wyrmias' attention. I fear that the only way
to save the town is to bring him what he asks for. If the town is to be saved,
you must do as he asks.
We are from the village of Gedron -- or what is left of it.
A defiler snuck into the town and took control of the mayor, and then the rest
of the town as well. He threatened to kill them if we did not leave and become
slaves.
It is south of here. I warn you that if you intend to go there, Wyrmias will
kill the village if you take any action against him. Please do not let him
No! The last time someone escaped, Wyrmias had that man's family burned
alive! It's not worth it!
All I know is that he's obsessed with some statue. He's a lunatic!
They're on another break. They know we won't try to escape. Wyrmias
would kill our families if we tried.
No. Wyrmias is a defiler, and he knows much more than what he sees. I will
not be the one that kills our families by trying something Wyrmias could find
out about, regardless of the odds.
Nothing would please me more than killing that monster! But, he would annihilate
our entire village with a single spell before we even got close.  There's no way.
I don't know. Ever since he came to the village he's been looking for
the missing pieces of the statue. I'm sure it is part of some evil design.
True, but I won't change my mind. If you want to attack the slavers,
go ahead -- we're not getting involved.
Thank you for freeing us.
Talk to our leader, Karas. You'll find him in the middle of the pen.
Karas speaks for all of us. He's in the middle of the pen.
We're behind you. Let's go.
Hey! Wait just a second! I want to talk to you!
What do you think you're doing with my gladiators?! Stop that!
No. They're free now.
You can't hold them any longer.
They're not your gladiators any more!
Take a loss and leave quietly.
Wyrmias is dead. You can't stop them.
You've really got to stop doing that.
Do you really think you can take us?
Oops! I'll put them back. Sorry.
Is that so? Look, I'm more than happy to sell them to you, but just taking them
like this not only makes me look bad, but I'm out a considerable expense! What would
you have me do?
Are you serious? Do you realize how much money I'd be out?! I think I'll just
tell Wyrmias about this -- he'll make them stay.
I wouldn't have to do it if these guards would pay attention instead of slacking off!
Now, are you going to stop this escape, or do I have to use force?
Karas interjects!
No! You will not take us! We are going back to our village -- even if we have to
kill you to get there!
Are you kidding?! My guards and I would take you out in a second! Yes, we'd...
really... take... you....
Arant looks over at one of his guards who is, as expected, dozing again.
Arant looks around for his men, and notices that they didn't follow him.
He sighs.
Oh, who am I kidding? You win. I'm getting out of here. As a matter of fact, here,
take my equipment -- I'm getting out of this line of work for good.
I can't thank you enough for what you've done. We're going to return to
Gedron now. Good luck to you in your travels.
Wh-what?! Dead? Oh, great!
Arant picks up a large rock and turns to a nearby guard....
You! Why wasn't I informed of this! You've been napping again, haven't you?!
Without waiting for a response, Arant hurls the rock at the guard!
Let that be a lesson to you!
No! Leave this area while you can!
Get out of my way, runt!
What kind of monsters are here?
I'm not afraid of any monster!
What happened to your companions?
Thanks for the warning, goodbye.
The area is beset with monsters! If you do not turn back, you will surely die, just
as my companions died.
You don't want to know! Forget about this place and never come back, because
you'll never leave if you stay.
Then you will soon learn fear! Not but a few strides behind me are a pair of mastyrials!
They were killed by a pack of Tohr-kreen.... I tell you, there's nothing but death here.
It's your life, so you can throw it away if you want. Don't say you
weren't warned, though!
I'm leaving now, and you would do well to leave also. Standing around just
gives the monsters more time to stalk you. Goodbye.
What do you say?
Do you wish to leave this area?
What do you do?
